subject: Atlas evaluation: checklist, owners, and approval lane
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@atlasretail.com>, Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@atlasretail.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 17 Aug 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Atlas evaluation: checklist, owners, and approval lane

Hi Samir / Lena —

Thanks again for the call today — appreciated the frank discussion about where Atlas is seeing friction with search latency and personalization variability. Quick recap of the pain/goals and a proposed checklist to keep decision makers aligned. Please review and confirm owners/dates below.

High-level pain points we captured:
- Average search-to-recommend latency spikes to ~600ms under peak; impacts conversion on mobile.
- Model drift on category synonyms (seasonal terms) causing poor recall for long-tail SKUs.
- Cost constraints: current endpoint spend makes multiple per-customer models challenging.

Primary goals for the evaluation:
1) Reduce 95th percentile latency to <200ms for SRCH endpoints.
2) Demonstrate stable relevance across promo season with a small eval set.
3) Establish a predictable cost baseline for production (tokens/embedding units).

Proposed checklist (mutual action plan style) — milestones, owner, target date:
- M1: Sandbox provisioning & test dataset upload — Owner: Atlas (Lena) — Target: 2026-08-21
- M2: Baseline latency + relevance report (Redwood) — Owner: Redwood (Neha/Ben) — Target: 2026-08-25
- M3: POC run (2-week) with quantized instances — Owner: Atlas/Redwood — Target start: 2026-08-28
- M4: Procurement & commercial terms finalization — Owner: Atlas procurement — Target: 2026-08-25 (kickoff), decision by 2026-09-10
- M5: Exec review & go/no-go — Owner: Atlas exec sponsor (Samir) — Target: 2026-09-10

Questions / asks for you today:
1) Confirm the primary decision maker(s) and procurement timeline (Samir noted exec review).
2) Can procurement@atlasretail.com be included on the kickoff?
3) Are there SLA availability targets we should include in the POC?

Attachments: redwood-mpa-draft.xlsx (MPA draft with milestone table), security-summary.pdf (SOC summary + data controls)

If that looks right I’ll drop the MPA into a shared Drive and schedule the kickoff for Aug 21.

Thanks —
Neha Kapoor
Enterprise Account Executive, Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0137

From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@atlasretail.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@atlasretail.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, procurement@atlasretail.com
Date: Mon, 17 Aug 2026 17:34:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Atlas evaluation: checklist, owners, and approval lane

Neha — thanks for the concise plan. A couple notes / clarifications from our side:

1) Decision makers: me (exec sponsor) + Cara Wilson (Head Product) for final sign-off. Cara is traveling this week but available for the exec review on 2026-09-10.
2) Procurement: I’ve looped procurement@atlasretail.com here — they’ll want a short SOW + pricing band before the kickoff. I attached our internal SOW template for your reference.
3) SLA ask: availability target should be 99.9% (monthly). We also want to see p95 latency in the dashboard and an agreed rollback plan if performance deviates during the POC.

Also — we’ll want a short 30–45 minute POC acceptance criteria review with our DevOps and Product owners before the POC starts. Can Ben/Marcus join that?

Attached: atlas-sow-template.docx

Samir
VP Engineering, Atlas Retail
samir.patel@atlasretail.com

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir.patel@atlasretail.com>, Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@atlasretail.com>, procurement@atlasretail.com
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 09:10:05 -0700
Subject: Re: Atlas evaluation: checklist, owners, and approval lane

Looping in Marcus for infra sizing and the p95 instrumentation. Marcus — noted the 99.9% availability ask and the p95 visibility requirement. I’ll prepare a short deck with expected throughput and GPU footprint for the POC (quantized instance) by EOD Aug 20.

Marcus — could you confirm: for a 2-week POC across 3 region replicas (US-EAST, US-WEST, EU), estimate the instance count and a ballpark monthly cost range? That will help Samir’s procurement team set expectations.

Thanks —
Ben
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir.patel@atlasretail.com>, Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@atlasretail.com>, procurement@atlasretail.com
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 11:22:37 -0700
Subject: Re: Atlas evaluation: checklist, owners, and approval lane

Ben / team — prelim estimates below (will formalize in the deck):
- POC config: 3 replicas (us-east, us-west, eu-west) each with 2x A10-like GPUs for throughput and to hit p95 <200ms with continuous batching.
- Expected observed token throughput for test dataset: ~40k tokens/minute across replicas.
- Ballpark POC cost (instance + infra + networking): $6k–$9k for full 2-week window (depends on quantization + caching enabled).

I’ll add a short runbook describing rollback/auto-fallback to a lower-cost model variant if p95 drifts. Sending the sizing deck by Aug 20 COB.

—Marcus
Infra & Performance, Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.com

From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@atlasretail.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@atlasretail.com>, procurement@atlasretail.com
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 17:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Atlas evaluation: checklist, owners, and approval lane

All — this looks good and aligns with internal expectations.

Confirmed next steps from Atlas:
- Procurement kickoff: Aug 25 (procurement@atlasretail.com) — procurement will own commercial negotiation.
- POC acceptance criteria review with DevOps & Product: Aug 26 (30–45m) — Samir & Cara to attend.
- Target decision date (exec review): Sep 10, 2026.

Samir — can Redwood send an initial SOW and a pricing band (three tiers: evaluation, pilot, production) by Aug 24 so procurement and our finance team can prep? If yes we’ll lock the kickoff.

Thanks everyone — looking forward to the POC.

Best,
Samir

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@atlasretail.com>, procurement@atlasretail.com
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@atlasretail.com>
Date: Wed, 19 Aug 2026 08:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Atlas evaluation: checklist, owners, and approval lane

Samir / procurement team — will do. We’ll circulate a concise SOW + three-tier pricing band by Aug 24 and lock the Aug 25 kickoff. Ben and Marcus will join the acceptance criteria review on Aug 26. I’ll send calendar invites and drop the MPA to the Drive link in my prior email.

Appreciate the quick alignment — Neha
